The current logic reuses the highest issue number after a purge. I need to persist a high-water mark so new issues always continue from the highest number ever used. Options include adding a column to the projects table, creating a separate table for purged numbers, or avoiding deletion of the highest-numbered issue.

I need to understand how migrations work and how tests set up the database.

The current `nextIssueNumber` logic uses `MAX(number)` from existing rows. Deleting the highest issue would allow that number to be reused. To prevent this, I am considering adding a `highest_issue_number` column to the projects table.

A separate `issue_number_counters` table was considered but rejected. Stubs or metadata were also dismissed because the issue must be deleted permanently. The existing comment in the issue repository confirms that archived issues keep their numbers, so the high-water mark must survive deletion.

/**
 * Brings `databasePath` up to date. Generated migrations win when they exist;
 * otherwise the embedded schema is pushed. Safe to run repeatedly — every
 * statement is `IF NOT EXISTS`.
 */
export async function runMigrations(
  databasePath: string = process.env.TASKFLOW_DB_PATH ?? DEFAULT_DB_PATH,
): Promise<void> {
  const absolute = resolve(process.cwd(), databasePath);
  mkdirSync(dirname(absolute), { recursive: true });

  const sqlite = new Database(absolute);
  sqlite.pragma("journal_mode = WAL");

  try {
    for (const statement of readMigrationStatements()) {
      sqlite.exec(statement);
    }
  } finally {
    sqlite.close();
  }
}

/** `pnpm db:migrate` runs this file directly; importing it must stay inert. */
if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith("migrate.ts") === true) {
  await runMigrations();
}

function readMigrationStatements(): readonly string[] {
  const dir = resolve(process.cwd(), MIGRATIONS_DIR);
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;

  const files = readdirSync(dir)
    .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".sql"))
    .sort();

  if (files.length === 0) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;

  return files.flatMap((name) =>
    readFileSync(join(dir, name), "utf8")
      .split("--> statement-breakpoint")
      .map((chunk) => chunk.trim())
      .filter(Boolean),
  );
}
